title: Web APIs: localStorage, sessionStorage, geolocation and notifications

videos.script:
A page forgets everything the moment it is closed. {{forget}} Variables, objects, the half-written review: gone on the next visit, unless the page asks the browser to keep it.

{{storage}} Browsers keep two small key-and-value stores for every site. localStorage remembers across visits, until someone clears it. sessionStorage remembers for one tab, until that tab is closed. Both hold text, and only text, which surprises everybody once.

{{rules}} Then the rules that go with them: which site can read what, how much fits, and the one kind of data that must never go there.

{{permission}} The second half is about things a page has to ask for. Where the user is. Whether it may show a notification when the tab is in the background. The browser stands between the page and the person, and the person decides.

{{lab}} The lab's browser cannot walk around São Paulo or show a notification on a screen it does not have, so this lesson says plainly which parts were staged and which were not run at all.
